description: What each school subject is, what it studies, how it thinks and why it matters. Shape: term, keywords, a (definition), points, example, why, related. Add entries here and run npm run check:brain.

entries.subject: History
entries.keywords: history historian past study of the past meaning definition subject
entries.a: History is the study of the past: what happened, when it happened, who was involved, and why it happened.
points: Historians use sources (documents, objects, photographs, oral stories) as evidence.
Events are placed in order on a timeline so we can see cause and effect.
History asks why things changed, not only what happened.
entries.example: The story of Great Zimbabwe, the First and Second Chimurenga and Independence in 1980 are all part of Zimbabwe's history.
entries.why: Knowing how we got here helps us understand the present and make wiser choices about the future.

entries.subject: Geography
entries.keywords: geography geographer places earth study of the earth meaning definition subject
entries.a: Geography is the study of the Earth: its land, water, climate and weather, and how people live with and change the places around them.
points: Physical geography: mountains, rivers, climate, soils, vegetation.
Human geography: towns, farming, population, trade, transport.
Geographers use maps, graphs and fieldwork to find patterns.
entries.example: Why Harare is cooler than Beitbridge, or why most farming happens in the Highveld, are geography questions.
entries.why: It explains where things are, why they are there, and how we can look after our environment.
related: How do I read a map?
What is the difference between weather and climate?

entries.subject: Mathematics
entries.keywords: mathematics maths math numbers study of numbers meaning definition subject
entries.a: Mathematics is the study of numbers, shapes, patterns and quantities, and the logical rules that connect them.
points: Number: counting, adding, fractions, percentages.
Algebra: using letters for unknown numbers.
Geometry: shapes, angles, area and volume.
Statistics: collecting and understanding data.
entries.example: Working out change at the tuckshop, or the area of a garden, uses mathematics.
entries.why: Maths trains clear step-by-step thinking and is used in money, building, science and technology.

entries.subject: Science
entries.keywords: science scientist scientific method study of nature meaning definition subject
entries.a: Science is a way of finding out how the natural world works by asking questions, testing ideas with experiments and trusting the evidence.
points: Biology studies living things, chemistry studies materials, physics studies energy and forces.
The scientific method: ask, predict, test, record, conclude.
A good test changes one thing at a time (a fair test).
entries.example: Planting beans in light and in the dark to see which grows better is a simple science experiment.
entries.why: Science gives us medicine, clean water, electricity and ways to protect the environment.

entries.subject: Biology
entries.keywords: biology biologist living things life study of life meaning definition subject
entries.a: Biology is the study of living things: plants, animals, people and tiny organisms, and how their bodies work and live together.
points: Living things move, respire, sense, grow, reproduce, excrete and need nutrition (MRS GREN).
Cells are the building blocks of life.
Ecosystems link living things with their environment.
entries.example: How a leaf makes food (photosynthesis) or how the heart pumps blood are biology topics.
entries.why: It helps us stay healthy, farm well and protect nature.

entries.subject: Chemistry
entries.keywords: chemistry chemist chemicals substances matter reactions study of matter meaning definition subject
entries.a: Chemistry is the study of matter: what substances are made of, how they behave and how they change into new substances.
points: Everything is made of atoms joined into elements and compounds.
A chemical change makes a new substance (rusting, burning, cooking).
Acids, bases and salts are common groups to compare.
entries.example: Iron rusting, bread baking and soap cleaning are chemistry in daily life.
entries.why: It lets us make medicine, fertiliser, clean water and new materials.

entries.subject: Physics
entries.keywords: physics physicist forces energy motion light electricity study of energy meaning definition subject
entries.a: Physics is the study of energy, forces, motion, light, sound, heat and electricity, and the rules that describe how the universe behaves.
points: Forces change how things move.
Energy changes form but is never lost.
Physics often uses measurements and formulas.
entries.example: Why a ball falls, how a solar panel works and why a bridge stays up are physics questions.
entries.why: It is the base of engineering, electricity and modern technology.

entries.subject: English
entries.keywords: english language grammar reading writing communication meaning definition subject
entries.a: English as a school subject teaches you to read, write, speak and listen well, and to understand how the language works (grammar, vocabulary and style).
points: Reading and comprehension: understanding what a text says and means.
Writing: essays, letters, reports and stories.
Grammar: nouns, verbs, tenses and sentence structure.
entries.example: Writing a formal letter to a headmaster or summarising a passage are English skills.
entries.why: Clear communication helps in every other subject and in work.

entries.subject: Literature
entries.keywords: literature novel poem poetry drama play story themes characters meaning definition subject
entries.a: Literature is written or spoken art such as novels, poems, plays and stories. Studying it means understanding characters, themes, setting, language and the author's message.
points: Theme: the big idea (for example justice or family).
Character: a person in the story and what drives them.
Figures of speech: simile, metaphor and personification add meaning.
entries.example: Explaining why a character makes a hard choice in a novel is a literature question.
entries.why: It builds empathy, imagination and the ability to read between the lines.

entries.subject: Shona
entries.keywords: shona chishona language chiShona subject meaning definition
entries.a: Shona (chiShona) is the most widely spoken first language in Zimbabwe. As a school subject it covers speaking, reading, writing, grammar, proverbs (tsumo), folktales (ngano) and poetry (nhetembo).
points: Proverbs carry traditional wisdom.
Greetings and respect (hunhu) are part of the language.
Writing follows set spelling rules.
entries.example: Mhoro means hello, and ndatenda means thank you.
entries.why: It keeps culture and identity strong and helps communication at home and in the community.

entries.subject: Ndebele
entries.keywords: ndebele isindebele language subject meaning definition
entries.a: Ndebele (isiNdebele) is a Zimbabwean language spoken mainly in Matabeleland. As a subject it covers speaking, reading, writing, grammar, proverbs (izaga) and folktales (izindaba).
points: Clicks and tone are part of the sound of the language.
Respect (inhlonipho) is a core value.
Written work follows set spelling and grammar rules.
entries.example: Sawubona means hello and ngiyabonga means thank you.
entries.why: It keeps culture alive and lets communities share knowledge across generations.

entries.subject: Social Studies and Heritage
entries.keywords: social studies heritage family and heritage studies culture society community citizens meaning definition subject
entries.a: Social Studies and Heritage Studies teach how people live together: culture, history, government, rights and responsibilities, and caring for our heritage and environment.
points: Learn about your family, community and nation.
Understand rights and responsibilities of citizens.
Protect heritage sites, traditions and the environment.
entries.example: Learning the national symbols and why we vote are social studies topics.
entries.why: It prepares learners to be informed, respectful citizens.

entries.subject: Agriculture
entries.keywords: agriculture farming crops livestock soil study of farming meaning definition subject
entries.a: Agriculture is the science and practice of growing crops and keeping animals for food, materials and income.
points: Crop production: soil, seeds, planting, weeding, harvesting.
Livestock: cattle, goats, poultry, feeding and health.
Sustainability: protecting soil and water for the future.
entries.example: Crop rotation, making compost and vaccinating chickens are agriculture topics.
entries.why: Zimbabwe's food, jobs and exports depend heavily on farming.

entries.subject: Business Studies
entries.keywords: business studies commerce enterprise entrepreneur trade meaning definition subject
entries.a: Business Studies teaches how businesses start, run and grow: money, marketing, records, teamwork and the law.
points: Entrepreneurs spot needs and make products or services.
Businesses must cover costs and aim for profit.
Good records show whether the business is doing well.
entries.example: Planning a tuckshop, setting prices and recording sales are business studies tasks.
entries.why: It builds the skills to start a small business or manage money well.

entries.subject: Accounts
entries.keywords: accounts accounting bookkeeping ledger records money meaning definition subject
entries.a: Accounting (accounts) is recording, summarising and reporting money matters so people can see income, expenses, assets and debts.
points: Double entry: every transaction has two sides.
Key reports: income statement and balance sheet.
Accuracy and honesty are essential.
entries.example: Writing down every sale and expense of a small shop and finding the profit is accounting.
entries.why: Without records a business cannot know if it is making money.

entries.subject: Economics
entries.keywords: economics economy scarcity choices resources production study of choices meaning definition subject
entries.a: Economics is the study of how people, businesses and governments choose to use limited resources to meet their needs and wants.
points: Scarcity: resources are limited, wants are not.
Every choice has an opportunity cost: the next best thing you give up.
Prices come from supply and demand.
entries.example: Choosing to spend your pocket money on a book instead of airtime has an opportunity cost.
entries.why: It explains prices, jobs, trade and why countries grow or struggle.

entries.subject: ICT and Computer Science
entries.keywords: ict computer science computing computers information technology digital meaning definition subject
entries.a: ICT and Computer Science teach how computers and digital tools store, process and share information, and how to use them safely and creatively.
points: Hardware is the physical parts; software is the programs.
Algorithms are step-by-step instructions to solve a problem.
Online safety: strong passwords, privacy and kindness.
entries.example: Typing a document, making a spreadsheet or writing a short program are ICT tasks.
entries.why: Almost every job and service now uses digital technology.

entries.subject: Religious Studies
entries.keywords: religious studies religion re divinity beliefs faith values meaning definition subject
entries.a: Religious Studies looks at the beliefs, texts, practices and values of different faiths, and how they guide people's lives and relationships.
points: Learn what different religions believe and why.
Explore values such as honesty, forgiveness and service.
Respect people of every belief.
entries.example: Comparing how different faiths celebrate thanksgiving is a religious studies topic.
entries.why: It builds understanding and respect in a diverse society.

entries.subject: Physical Education
entries.keywords: physical education pe sport exercise fitness health games meaning definition subject
entries.a: Physical Education (PE) teaches fitness, sport skills, teamwork and healthy habits through movement.
points: Warm up before and cool down after exercise.
Sport teaches fair play and teamwork.
Regular activity strengthens the heart and mind.
entries.example: Netball drills, athletics and stretching are part of PE.
entries.why: A fit body helps you concentrate and stay well.
related: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?

entries.subject: Art and Design
entries.keywords: art design drawing painting craft sculpture creative visual arts meaning definition subject
entries.a: Art and Design develops creativity through drawing, painting, craft, sculpture and design, and teaches you to observe carefully and express ideas.
points: Elements of art: line, shape, colour, texture, pattern.
Design solves a problem and looks good.
Zimbabwean stone sculpture is world famous.
entries.example: Making a poster or a clay pot uses art and design skills.
entries.why: It builds imagination, patience and problem solving.

entries.subject: Music
entries.keywords: music rhythm melody singing instruments mbira performance subject meaning definition
entries.a: Music is organised sound. In school you learn to sing, play instruments, read rhythm and melody, and enjoy music from different cultures.
points: Rhythm is the beat pattern; melody is the tune.
Traditional instruments include the mbira, hosho and ngoma.
Choirs and groups teach teamwork.
entries.example: Clapping a steady beat while singing a song is a music activity.
entries.why: It builds listening, memory and confidence and keeps culture alive.

entries.subject: Design and Technology
entries.keywords: design and technology technical graphics woodwork metalwork building engineering making meaning definition subject
entries.a: Design and Technology teaches you to design, make and test useful things, from drawings to finished products, using tools, materials and safe methods.
points: Follow the design process: need, ideas, plan, make, test, improve.
Choose materials for strength, cost and looks.
Safety rules protect you and others.
entries.example: Designing and building a small wooden stool.
entries.why: It leads to careers in building, engineering and manufacturing.

entries.subject: Environmental Science
entries.keywords: environment environmental science conservation ecology pollution sustainability meaning definition subject
entries.a: Environmental Science studies how living things and their surroundings affect each other, and how people can protect land, water and air.
points: Human actions such as deforestation and pollution harm ecosystems.
Conservation means using resources wisely.
Reduce, reuse, recycle.
entries.example: Planting trees to stop soil erosion is an environmental action.
entries.why: A healthy environment gives us food, water and a safe home.
related: Why does cutting down trees cause soil erosion?
